record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.context_brief: mapping class groups and Property T
record.original_question: For a closed oriented surface of genus g ≥ 2, does its mapping class group satisfy Kazhdan's Property T?

evidence.quote: Does the mapping class group of a surface of genus g ≥ 2 satisfy Kazhdan's Property T?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ denote its mapping class group, i.e., the group of isotopy classes of orientation-preserving self-homeomorphisms of $\Sigma_g$. Recall that a discrete countable group $\Gamma$ has Kazhdan's Property (T) if every unitary representation of $\Gamma$ on a Hilbert space that has almost invariant vectors (i.e., for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every finite subset $F \subset \Gamma$ there exists a unit vector $v$ with $\|\pi(\gamma)v - v\| < \varepsilon$ for all $\gamma \in F$) must have a nonzero invariant vector. Determine whether $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ has Kazhdan's Property (T).
artifact.status_search_result: J. E. Andersen (2007) proved that the mapping class group of a closed oriented surface of genus g ≥ 2 does not have Kazhdan's Property (T), answering the question in the negative. An earlier partial result by Taherkhani handled the genus-2 case via cofinite subgroups with non-vanishing first cohomology.

status_evidence.title: Mapping Class Groups do not have Kazhdan's Property (T)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the mapping class group of a closed oriented surface of genus at least two does not have Kazhdan's property (T).
status_evidence.claim: Andersen proved Mod(Σ_g) does not have Property (T) for g ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: The Kazhdan property of the mapping class group of closed surfaces ...
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs finite-index subgroups of the genus-2 mapping class group with non-vanishing first cohomology, showing failure of Property (T).
status_evidence.claim: Taherkhani showed the genus-2 mapping class group fails Property (T).
